summary: Gone Jefferson County, Indiana, DNR fire tower on IN-7 northwest of Madison; only footers remained at a June 2024 visit; no construction date found.

facts.status_note: Not standing; footers still exist as of June 2024 (Indiana Fire Towers).

visit.trail_note: The Indiana Fire Towers author drove to the site in June 2024 and found the footers near a National Geodetic Survey mark.

events.note: A 1936 county map shows no fire tower at the site. The Indiana Fire Towers author reads that as suggesting the tower did not yet exist (an inference, not a dated record).
June 2024 visit: not standing; footers found near a National Geodetic Survey mark said to be about ten meters from the old tower

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Two reference points, not a contradiction: Indiana Fire Towers places the site on IN-7 northwest of Madison, and the Forest Service table names Lancaster as the nearest town. The story reports both with their sources.

notes_for_editor: Only three sources, and two of them are short lists. No source read gives a builder, height, construction date, staffing, fires, or removal date, so the story leaves those out. The 1936 map point is the Indiana Fire Towers author's inference and is labelled that way. Ownership and public access are not stated in any source read, so the access key is omitted. The Forest Lookouts page for Five Points gives only 'Indiana - Jefferson County'. A search summary's estimate of the tower's distance from Volga was our own rough calculation with no source, and it is not used. Five Points Fire Museum in Lafayette is a different place and is not relevant. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the 'almost all in the southern portion' line, the Forest Service nearest-town column, and the county and June 2024 visit details were added to evidence. The story's footnote naming the Forest Fire Lookout Association list was corrected, and the 'only the footers remain' line is now dated to June 2024.
